title: Marginalia
oneLiner: Ask a question about a PDF corpus and get claims whose quotes are verbatim, highlighted on the page, with an inspectable retrieval trace and a calibrated refusal.
previewCommand: uv run docqa serve --port 8788  # then, in a second shell: npm --prefix ui run dev

shots.alt: Marginalia over the Sentence-BERT paper: citation 2 selected, its verbatim quote highlighted on PDF page 2 with a margin marker, and the matching source row in the answer pane. Seeded offline demo data; no model call.
Citation view for the sentence-embedding question: the selected source quote is highlighted on PDF page 3, beside claims 1-3 and the source list. Seeded offline demo data; no model call.

Retrieval trail at the second-pass cross-encoder section: rerank rank, score, calibrated evidence probability, kept status, then the final context and decision. Recorded demo trace, not a live request.
Evaluation view of the committed eval-report.json: 2 of 5 checks met, counts and denominators, Wilson 95% ranges, and the stage where each question stopped.

invariants.claim: Ingest refuses a chunk longer than 448 model tokens rather than storing a truncated vector.
A claim without an in-context citation, or whose quote is not a normalised substring of the cited chunk, is dropped.
Ingest refuses a PDF whose SHA-256 differs from corpus.lock.json.
The refusal threshold comes from eval/calibration.json at boot and is never hand-tuned.
Every rate carries a Wilson 95% interval and its denominator; the eval records the earliest stage that produced no answer for each question.
The judge model differs from the generator and is pinned by exact id; its reliability is recorded by the judge check.
ONNX work runs in a worker thread behind Semaphore(2).

limits: The free endpoint answered 8/24 answerable questions.
Citation precision and faithfulness are rule-based, rest on n=9, and reach down to 45.3%.
The calibration is fitted in-sample on the same 30 eval questions.
The eval set is 30 questions (24 answerable, 6 unanswerable); the intervals are wide.
